The whole platform in one map

A source-linked technical walkthrough. Trace the flow, explain the boundary, then test the failure path.

After this session, you can:
  • Place every LoanOS surface and runtime
  • Explain the four product planes
  • Trace one request from channel to evidence

Technical flow

Every hand-off is a control boundary: on failure the flow holds, refers or denies — it never skips ahead.

  1. 01Borrower / staff / partner channel
  2. 02Node API and domain services
  3. 03Per-tenant business + control engines
  4. 04Tenant store and audit chain
  5. 05Evidence, reports and operations

1. The product shape

LoanOS is an India-only, multi-tenant lending operating system.

LOS originates credit, LMS owns the live account, LWS coordinates human work, and the compliance control plane makes policy, evidence and model governance executable.

These are product planes, not four disconnected products.

2. Two runtimes, one governed system

The Node control/data plane owns HTTP workflows, tenant state and the audit chain.

The pure-Rust decision plane evaluates signed policy bundles deterministically.

The boundary is deliberate: workflow code asks for a decision; it does not quietly reimplement policy.

3. How to read the repository

Front ends live under apps/.

Domain controls live in the @loanos/core workspace package (packages/core/), grouped into domain folders — compliance, lending, finance, identity, ai, journeys, integrations, platform, operations and shared — and consumed only through the package boundary, never by relative path (ADR 0008).

The API composes those controls in apps/api/.

Rust policy execution lives under rules/.

PostgreSQL schema and RLS live under db/.

Architecture, product maturity and regulatory claims remain governed documents under docs/.
